I found one real bug in `black.strings`: a regex denial-of-service (catastrophic backtracking) in `lines_with_leading_tabs_expanded`. This is CVE-2024-21503. The report is at `runs/black_r3/bug_report_black_strings_2026-10-06_01-20_synj.md`.

**The bug (High severity):** the pattern `FIRST_NON_WHITESPACE_RE = r"\s*\t+\s*(\S)"` gets very slow on a line made only of tabs or whitespace. The three parts all match tab characters, so when the match finally fails the regex engine tries a huge number of splits. Time grows roughly with the cube of the line length:

| Tabs on the line | Time |
|---|---|
| 250 | 0.05 s |
| 500 | 0.42 s |
| 1,000 | 3.3 s |
| 2,000 | 25.7 s |

Black runs this function on every docstring, so it can be triggered by ordinary input. I confirmed it end-to-end: running `black.format_str` on a function whose docstring contains 1,000 tabs took 3.2 s. Hypothesis found the problem at 275 tabs, using a 0.1 s time limit. The report includes a fix that finds the leading whitespace with `lstrip()` instead of the regex, which takes linear time. I wrote the fix but did not apply it or run the tests against it.

**Minor inconsistency, not reported:** `str_width` counts every ASCII character as width 1, but `char_width` says control characters like `'\x1f'` have width 0. So `str_width('\x1f')` returns 1 while `char_width('\x1f')` returns 0, and `count_chars_in_width` (which uses `char_width`) disagrees with `str_width`. This comes from a deliberate fast path for ASCII text, and control characters rarely appear in source lines.

**Properties that passed:**
- `normalize_string_quotes` keeps the string's value and gives the same result if run twice.
- `normalize_string_prefix` keeps the string's value.
- `lines_with_leading_tabs_expanded` keeps the line count and each line's content.
- `count_chars_in_width` returns the most characters that fit in the given width.
- `fix_docstring` gives the same result if run twice.

One failure along the way was my own test's fault, not Black's: my generator produced `'a'''`, which Python reads as two strings stuck together. I fixed the generator to produce only single string literals.

The tests are in `runs/black_r3/test_strings.py`.

Several claude.ai connectors (Asana, Atlassian, Box, Canva, Figma, HubSpot, Intercom, Linear, Notion, monday.com) need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings before they can be used. None of them were needed for this.
